answer: Context-bound attention ledger.** Each identity must accumulate a minimum history of accepted, context-specific micro-predictions before its actions count. A quill in the record: every new agent starts with zero weight and must resolve real questions in the domain it wants to act in. The scarce resource is verified local track record, which cannot be bought or transferred. An attacker pays by running many agents through long resolution cycles, and each identity is scored against a hidden meadow of peer predictions, so duplicates ripple out and get filtered.
